plan.contextChunk: This figure is a coordinate plane carrying four straight lines, each in a different color with arrowheads on both ends and tagged with a Roman numeral. The horizontal axis is labeled x and numbered from -7 to 7, the vertical axis is labeled y and numbered from -5 to 5, and a light gray unit grid fills the plotting region. Line I is orange and by far the steepest, rising from below the x-axis at the lower left and exiting through the top of the grid just right of the y-axis, where its label sits. Line II is light blue and the shallowest, entering at the left near x equal to -6.5 on the x-axis, crossing the y-axis at 3, and climbing to about x equal to 4, y equal to 5. Line III is teal, crossing the y-axis at -3 and the x-axis near x equal to 1.5 before rising to that same upper right region. Line IV is dark blue and the only line with a negative slope, entering at the upper left, crossing the y-axis at 3, and descending to roughly x equal to 4, y equal to -4.5. Color and numeral identify the lines, leaving steepness and direction as the properties to read off. The plot supports an exercise in pairing four given linear equations with the correct lines.

interactionPlan.concept: A line's equation y = mx + b is fully determined by its slope m (steepness and direction) and y-intercept b (where it crosses the vertical axis), and these two parameters can be read directly from the graph.
elements: x-axis labeled 'x' with tick marks from -7 to 7
y-axis labeled 'y' with tick marks from -5 to 5
light gray unit grid filling the plotting region
Line I: orange, slope 5, y-intercept 3, arrowheads on both ends, label 'I' near upper right
Line II: light blue, slope 0.5, y-intercept 3, arrowheads on both ends, label 'II' near upper right
Line III: teal, slope 2, y-intercept -3, arrowheads on both ends, label 'III' near upper right
Line IV: dark blue, slope -2, y-intercept 3, arrowheads on both ends, label 'IV' near lower right
Candidate line: dashed magenta/purple, controlled by sliders, with a small dot at its y-intercept
Rise-over-run markers: right-triangle overlay (horizontal run segment and vertical rise segment) shown on the clicked line

interactions.label: Slope m
interactions.teaches: Changing m rotates the candidate line around its y-intercept — positive m tilts it up-right, negative m tilts it down-right, and larger |m| makes it steeper, directly matching the visual steepness of lines I–IV

interactions.label: y-intercept b
interactions.teaches: Changing b slides the candidate line vertically without altering its angle — the dot on the y-axis moves to b, showing that lines with the same slope but different intercepts are parallel shifts of each other
Clicking a labeled line reveals its rise-over-run triangle, making the abstract slope value concrete: the ratio of vertical change to horizontal change between two lattice points on that line

demo_steps.title: Four lines, two parameters
demo_steps.narration: Four lines share the same coordinate plane. Lines I, II, and IV all cross the y-axis at 3 but fan out at different angles; line III crosses at −3. The two numbers that distinguish them are slope and y-intercept.

demo_steps.title: Read the slope visually
demo_steps.narration: Click line IV (dark blue). A right-triangle overlay appears showing a run of 1 and a rise of −2, confirming slope = −2. Click line I (orange) to see its much steeper rise-over-run of 5/1.

demo_steps.title: Match slope, then intercept
demo_steps.narration: Set the slope slider to 2 — the candidate line now has the same angle as line III but sits too high. Drag the y-intercept slider down to −3 and the candidate line lands exactly on line III, confirming y = 2x − 3.

demo_steps.title: Same intercept, different slopes
demo_steps.narration: Set b = 3 and sweep the slope slider from −2 through 0.5 to 5. The candidate line pivots through lines IV, II, and I in sequence — all three share the y-intercept 3 but are distinguished entirely by slope.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Every line on the plane is uniquely identified by just two numbers — where it crosses the y-axis (b) and how steeply it rises or falls (m) — and both can be read directly from the graph.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Standard Cartesian grid with light gray unit squares, bold black axes with arrowheads. Line I orange (#E8611A), Line II light blue (#5BA3D9), Line III teal (#1A9E8F), Line IV dark navy (#1B3A6B). Each line has small arrowheads at both visible ends and a Roman numeral label near its upper-right terminus (IV's label near lower-right). The candidate line should be dashed magenta (#C0399A) with a filled dot at (0, b) to anchor the y-intercept visually. Rise-over-run markers: a horizontal segment (run) in the line's color and a vertical segment (rise) in a contrasting shade, forming a right triangle with a small square at the right-angle corner. Grid spans x ∈ [-7, 7], y ∈ [-5, 5].
